###chapter 1
Chloe stared at the stranger in the hotel vanity mirror. The white gown was a masterpiece. Hair pinned up tight, a heavy veil pooling around her heels, exposing just a hint of bare shoulder. Around her throat, a diamond choker caught the harsh light, blindingly bright.

The glam squad and her bridesmaids were buzzing, throwing out cheap praise. 

"Oh my god, literally a Disney princess," one squealed. 

"You're going to be the happiest girl alive today, babe."

Chloe’s mouth twitched into a cold, dead smirk. Yeah, right. If this were her first lifetime—before Ethan ditched her for his ex, before she ended up dead—maybe she’d actually believe the fairytale. Maybe she’d be swooning over her dream guy. But she knew better now. No do-overs in the real world.

*Click.* 

The heavy suite door swung wide. Ethan walked in like he owned the place. God, he looked the part. Tall, sharp jaw, eyes dark and full of secrets. He practically oozed that practiced, rich-boy charm.

The girls got the hint, shuffling out the door with quiet murmurs. 

"You ready yet?" Ethan checked his watch, his eyes darting to her. His voice carried a sharp edge of annoyance.

Chloe turned around slowly, keeping her voice level. "How do I look?"

He gave her a half-second shrug. Before his mouth could form a word, his pocket vibrated. He whipped out his phone. *Seraphina Vale* lit up the screen.

"We walk down the aisle in five minutes," Chloe said, her voice dropping. "Can you just... not answer that?"

"Don't start, Chloe," Ethan snapped, already tapping the screen. "Seraphina knows what day it is. If she's calling, it's a damn emergency."

He pressed the phone to his ear, ignoring her completely. His forehead creased into deep lines as he listened. He hung up a second later, his face pale. 

"Seraphina’s in trouble. I gotta go. Handle the guests for a bit." He spun on his heel.

Chloe lunged, grabbing his sleeve. "Ethan, stop. It's our wedding day. Who matters more here? Me, or her?"

"She's more important than my own damn life, Chloe! I owe her everything."

"Then what the hell am I to you?"

"Drop the drama, okay? A wedding is just a party, Chloe. You can handle the crowd. Seraphina actually needs me right now!"

A dry, hollow laugh slipped past her lips, though her eyes burned with pure, cold disgust. "A wedding without a groom, Ethan? Really? What, should I just prop up a picture of you at the altar?"

He shoved her hand off his arm. "I said drop it! Every single time Seraphina needs help, you throw a tantrum. Grow up and be reasonable for once!"

Chloe froze. Her face went completely blank. "Reasonable?" She exhaled slowly, locking eyes with him. "Fine. Walk out that door, and I'll just grab some other guy to stand at the altar with me." She took a step back, folding her arms.

Ethan scoffed. He figured she was just blowing off steam. She always barked, but she always crawled back. He threw the door open and walked out.

Five minutes later, the door banged open. Willow burst in, flanked by Chloe's parents, Walter and Beatrix. Willow’s eyes flared with a sick, twisted satisfaction when she saw Chloe standing alone, but she wiped it instantly. Her parents didn't catch a thing. Willow was a pro at playing the sweet girl—Chloe knew that act by heart.

"Chloe, oh my god, where's Ethan?" Willow gasped, her voice dripping with fake panic. "The ceremony is starting, and I just saw his car tear out of the parking lot! I mean, ever since his ex crawled back, he's been totally checked out. Is he calling it off? Everyone is waiting out there—not just family, but all of Dad's major investors! If this wedding tanks, the Sterling family name is trash." 

Willow let out a heavy, dramatic sigh. "Chloe... did you pick a fight with him?" She tilted her head, wearing her best pity face. "Seriously, you need to go apologize and fix this."

###chapter 2
"Seriously, Elara? Did you scare Ethan off again?" Beatrix barked, her voice dripping with that same old bossy tone. "Why can't you just act like Coraline for five minutes? You always gotta screw things up. You begged to marry the guy, and now that the day is here, you can't even keep him around. Guests are arriving, and the groom is literally missing. Do you have any idea how bad this makes us look?"

Elara kept her mouth shut. She just stared right through them, totally blank. It was her first time facing them since she died and woke up back in time.

Of course. They only noticed her when their precious reputation was on the line. Any other day, she could have dropped dead and they wouldn't have blinked.

She remembered her first life—bleeding out, begging them on the phone, while they laughed and popped champagne for Coraline’s massive birthday bash. Their adopted golden child got a party; Elara got a grave. Coraline's cake day was the day Elara died.

"God, Elara, just give it a rest," Beatrix groaned, throwing her hands up. "You’re dragging us through the mud, and Coraline too. Look, you’re both our girls. I don't expect you to be perfect like her, but is it too much to ask for you to not ruin everything?"

Elara’s face didn't twitch. "Relax. The wedding is happening. Go wait in the hall."

Walter squinted at her, gave a stiff nod, and dragged his wife out the door.

The second the door clicked, Coraline sneered. She leaned close, her breath hot on Elara’s ear. "Have fun being the biggest joke in the city today, sis. No groom. Ethan ditched you for Seraphina Vale. He’s gone for the weekend, babe."

*Crack.*

Elara’s palm hit Coraline’s cheek hard. Coraline stumbled back, grabbing her face, eyes popping out of her head.

"Are you freaking crazy?!" Coraline shrieked, rubbing the red mark.

Elara didn't flinch. Her eyes were pure ice. "Yeah. I am. And trust me, I’m just getting started."

Coraline shivered. Something was off. This wasn't the quiet, pathetic little sister she always pushed around. Elara had spent her whole life playing second fiddle, letting Coraline steal the spotlight.

Not today. The girl standing here was different. Cold. Deadly.

...

Elara turned on her heel, walked out, and marched down the hall to a different suite.

Alaric and Dominic were waiting inside. Alaric, the grandpa, was old but still sharp as a whip. Then there was Julian—Ethan’s uncle. He was the adopted baby of the Baker family, but now he ran the whole damn show. The guy was the king of Capitalton. Everyone feared him, everyone bowed to him, except maybe Alaric.

"The kid ran, huh?" Alaric asked, his white hair shaking as he grinned.

Elara nodded. "Is our deal still on?"

"You saved my life," Julian said from the couch. He locked his eyes on her—heavy, dark, and intense enough to make a grown man sweat. "If you're down, I'm down." No wonder the city was terrified of him.

"Ethan’s an idiot. He’ll learn the hard way," Alaric grunted, pushing himself up. "Julian, do the swap with Callie. Wipe Ethan out of the picture. If she wants you, you treat her right. Let's get this wedding started."

The old man sighed and walked out.

Just the two of them now.

Elara peeked at him, then quickly looked away. Dominic was a ghost, a beast, the most dangerous man in the city. One look from him could pull you in and crush you all at once.

###chapter 3
Elara started plotting this exact day—her wedding—exactly four weeks ago.

That was the day she woke up with a second shot at life. She already knew the script. Ethan would dump her for his "soulmate," leaving her to be the town's favorite joke.

So, she micromanaged every single detail of this wedding like a chess grandmaster.

But remembering her past life still made her blood boil and her chest ache. She never expected to end up as a tragic headline.

Marrying Ethan had been a total nightmare from day one. The guy was a ghost. Birthdays, anniversaries, major holidays—he spent every single one with Seraphina Vale. Elara just sat alone in an empty house, taking his cold shoulder and nasty remarks. Then, everything went to hell.

It happened right before her birthday.

Actually, Elara hadn't had a real birthday since Coraline invaded the Jewell family. Coraline’s birthday was a day before hers, so their parents always threw these massive "joint" parties. Total BS. Coraline was always the star, and Elara was just background noise.

She hadn't blown out her own candles since she was seven.

Then, right before another forgotten birthday, she got snatched. Kidnapped. Terrified, she called Ethan, begging for help. But he was with Seraphina. He literally yelled at her to stop annoying him and hung up. Panicking, she called her parents. Then her three brothers.

Nobody gave a shit.

"Elara, seriously? What kind of BS stunt are you pulling now?" they said.

"God, Elara, grow up. Why can't you be more like Coraline?" they said.

"Ugh, this is why we can't stand you. You're so damn selfish!" they said.

"Oh, you're in danger? Prove it! You always try to drag Coraline, but she’s literally ten times better than you!" they said.

So, Elara died. They tortured her to death and dumped her body like garbage.

Even after a month back in her own skin, those final, dark days still gave her the chills. Just thinking about it made her skin crawl. She couldn't go back to that headspace.

After she died, she floated around as a ghost for a while.

That’s how she found out Coraline was the one who set up the kidnapping. Coraline sold her to those monsters just so she could be the only precious "Jewell" in the family.

Since day one, Coraline had been playing the long game—sucking up to their parents and brothers while secretly making Elara's life a living hell.

She played the sweet, innocent victim, slowly poisoning Elara's relationship with everyone she loved.

And their parents bought it every time. They never believed a word Elara said. Instead, they called her a liar, a bully, and a jealous bitch.

Even her three brothers, who used to worship her, flipped and chose Coraline.

Never mind that Elara was the one who fixed her oldest brother's busted legs, saved her second brother's life, and basically made her youngest brother a superstar.

None of that crap mattered now.

To them, Coraline was the saint.

And when they finally heard she was dead? No tears. They basically figured she got what she deserved, dirty and ruined as she was.

They left her body to rot until Rowan Grey finally tracked her down. And it was Julian who dragged her out of that hellhole.

Julian handled the funeral. He was the only one who actually cried for her, sitting by her casket for days and nights.

###chapter 4
She bet everything on Julian. The guy literally owed her his life. He’d promised her a blank check—any favor, anytime. Just their little secret.

So, the second she woke up in this new life, she went straight to his place. 

"I need a favor," she said, and dumped the whole crazy plan on him.

If Ethan wanted to play games and skip the wedding, fine. Canceling wasn't an option, so she’d just upgrade. Big time.

Julian didn't even blink. He said yes, then went and handled Alaric for her. Alaric always spoiled her rotten anyway. Sure, she’d begged for this wedding in the first place, but now she wanted Julian instead of Ethan. If Julian was cool with it, Alaric wasn't going to argue.

"You sure about this, kid?" Julian asked. 

He stood up, and *damn*. The guy was six-foot-three of pure muscle, broad shoulders tapering down to a ridiculously lean waist, all wrapped in a custom-tailored suit. He didn't even have to try; he just radiated power.

"Positive," Elara said, nodding.

Inside, though? Her stomach was doing backflips.

Yeah, she’d saved his life once—that was his "debt." But Julian Baker wasn't some random dude. He was the terrifying boss of the Baker empire. The whole city of Capitalton walked on eggshells around him.

When she first pitched the "marry me" idea, she figured he'd laugh her out of the room. Instead, he signed up and cleared it with Alaric.

Oh, and did she mention he was Ethan’s uncle?

Stealing the nephew's wedding to marry the uncle? The media was going to have a field day.

But Julian just shrugged it off. "Let them talk," he’d said. "Nobody has the balls to say it to my face."

Julian offered his arm. "Let's go."

She looped her arm through his, and they walked toward the grand ballroom doors.

The venue staff had worked fast. The massive posters of her and Ethan at the entrance were already gone, replaced by shots of her and Julian.

She’d originally suggested a quick Photoshop job, but Julian had shut that down. He’d dragged her to a real, high-end photoshoot. Thank God he did.

Inside, the guests still had no clue.

Walter, who was supposed to walk her down the aisle, turned around and instantly froze.

There stood Julian, looking every bit the groom.

"M-Mr. Myers?" Walter stammered, his face turning pale. "What the hell are you doing?"

"The groom's job," Elara said, chin up. "And don't worry about walking me in. We've got this covered."

"Elara, what kind of stunt is this? Where is Ethan?"

"You're confused," Elara said. "I'm marrying Julian. Why would Ethan even be here?"

Walter’s brain short-circuited.

"Don't believe me?" Elara pointed. "See for yourself."

Walter looked over. Right there on the welcome board was Julian, looking insanely sharp in a tux, his name printed right next to hers in elegant gold script.

Walter practically lunged at the poster, staring at the print, then whipping his head back to Julian, then back to the poster. He looked like he’d seen a ghost.

Right then, Coraline sauntered out. She spotted Elara holding Julian’s arm, and her eyes flared for a split second before she slapped on a fake, sweet smile.

"Elara, sweetie, still no sign of Ethan?"

She tilted her head, acting all worried. "What are you going to do? You can't seriously walk down the aisle alone. You'll be the laughingstock of the city. Like, who even gets married without a groom? I mean, Ethan's kind of a jerk anyway, running off with his little soulmate. But seriously... what's your plan now?"

###chapter 5
Coraline squeezed her face into a fake-sad pout, but her heart was doing backflips. She couldn't wait for Elara to crash and burn. Once this trainwreck hit, the Jewells would throw Elara straight into the social gutter.

"Wait, no groom?" Elara scoffed, tossing her head. "Who said that? My guy is standing right next to me."

Right on cue, the DJ's voice boomed through the mic: "Alright, folks, let's hear it for the bride and groom!"

The double doors swung wide. Julian and Elara stepped through, gliding down the aisle like they owned the place.

The room went dead silent, then exploded into a wave of gasps.

"Hold up—isn't she marrying Ethan?"

"Wait, is that Julian?"

"Holy crap, Julian is the groom?"

"Where the hell is Ethan?"

Necks craned. People scanned the room, hunting for the missing guy. But the spotlight locked onto the main stage. Hand in hand, Elara and Julian looked like a million bucks.

Elara flashed a bright, sugary smile. "Hey, thanks for coming to celebrate me and Julian today! I hear some whispering about Ethan. Just a quick heads-up—Julian is the groom. Keep bringing up that loser Ethan, and my new husband might get a little cranky."

Nobody messed with Julian. The guy was a shark, cold and brutal, and everyone knew it. They feared him too much to push. The groom-swap made zero sense, but Elara’s little warning shut everyone up instantly.

Behind them, the massive LED screen flickered. Boom—giant wedding photos of Elara and Julian lit up the stage.

The crowd buzzed again, a low hum of pure shock. Heads turned toward Alaric, trying to read his face.

Over at their table, Coraline and her folks sat frozen, jaws on the floor.

"Mom, Dad... what the hell is this?" Coraline hissed. "Wasn't she marrying Ethan? Why is she up there on screen with Mr. Myers?"

Coraline scowled. Dominic. The ultimate, untouchable bachelor in the city. The guy she’d been drooling over for years. And now he was standing at the altar with Elara? What kind of sick joke was this?

Walter and Beatrix stared, totally blindsided. Their three sons looked at each other, completely clueless.

Even with everyone’s brains melting, the show went on. The schedule was locked. The DJ nailed every cue, and the whole ceremony wrapped up without a single glitch.

The second the crowd started to leave, Walter and Beatrix stormed over to Elara, looking ready to kill.

"Are you insane, Elara?" Beatrix snapped, her voice sharp. "Where is Ethan? He was supposed to be up there!"

"Yeah, what gives? Where's Ethan?" her three brothers chimed in, glaring.

Coraline’s brain did some quick math, and then it clicked. "Oh, I get it. Ethan bailed, so Mr. Myers stepped in to save face and stop a total PR disaster."

It made perfect sense. Why else would a god like Dominic stoop down to Elara's level?

She was engaged to his nephew, for God's sake. Marrying her would be a massive scandal. Even Alaric didn't stop it, so it had to be damage control.

Coraline smirked, proud of her own genius. She turned to Julian, waiting for him to back her up.

"Got a problem with me being Callie's husband?" Julian said, his voice smooth as silk. "Too bad. We're already hitched."

He grabbed Elara’s hand, flashing their matching wedding bands.

Coraline froze. Those weren't the rings Elara and Ethan had picked out. Not even close.

###chapter 6
"Callie's done for the night. We're out," Julian barked. He didn't wait for a reply. He just grabbed Elara's arm and hauled her through the crowd, ignoring the burning stares behind them. 

Near the exit, they almost ran right into Rowan Grey and her crew. 

Elara leaned in, keeping her voice low. "Hey, I'll text you the details later. Seriously, just go home."

The car door clicked shut. Elara sneaked a look at Julian. 

"Look, you can just drop me at a hotel," she muttered. The guilt was eating her alive. Sure, the contract was signed. Yeah, they were getting the marriage license tomorrow. But she still felt like a massive pain in his ass. 

Julian didn't even look up from his iPad. His fingers tapped out another work email. "You're Mrs. Myers now. Deal with it," he said, his voice cold and flat.

The tires crunched on the gravel of Myers Manor. The Capitalton estate was freaking huge. Elara had stood here once with Ethan, but tonight, the place felt totally different. 

Julian pushed the front door open and nudged her inside. 

"Martha!" he called out. The housekeeper appeared. "This is Mrs. Myers. She gets whatever she wants. I have to handle some business, so I'm heading out. Get her settled." 

Boom. Just like that, Julian vanished back into the night. Martha gave her a warm smile and led her upstairs to Julian's bedroom. It was exactly what she expected: minimalist, spotless, and zero clutter.

Elara woke up to an empty bed. She padded downstairs, and right on cue, the front door swung open. Julian walked in. 

"Morning," she said, trying to play it cool. 

"Morning," he muttered. 

The tension in the room was thick enough to cut with a knife. 

"Martha made food. Eat up. I'm going to jump in the shower, and then we're going to get that license," he said, already halfway up the stairs.

Elara let out a long, shaky breath. Her chest actually ached from holding it in. This house, this guy, this crazy new reality—it was a lot to take in. 

She slumped into a kitchen chair, but before she could even touch her food, her phone buzzed. Beatrix. 

"Elara! Get your butt back to this house right now and explain yesterday!" her mother shrieked. *Click.* She hung up.

Elara stared at the blank screen, then tossed the phone onto the table. 

Fine. She'd go back. Not for them—screw them—but to grab her stuff. Once she packed her bags today, she was done with that place forever. 

It was never a home anyway. They didn't even put her in the family portrait. The thought made her stomach twist with pure rage and a hollow kind of grief. 

She had spent her whole life playing the good girl, begging for crumbs. And for what? Her dad, Walter, her mom, Beatrix, and her three brothers didn't give a rat's ass about her. To them, Coraline was the golden child. The chosen one. Coraline got the designer bags and the hugs; Elara got the leftovers. 

She had nearly killed herself trying to make them love her. But dying—actually staring death in the face—changes a person. It clears the fog. If your own blood doesn't care if you breathe or bleed, they aren't family. They're just strangers.

###chapter 7
They grabbed a quick bite, then hit the courthouse. Boom. Just like that, they had the marriage license. 

Stepping out onto the pavement, Elara turned to him. "Hey, Uncle Julian, look. I know you've got a million things to do. We got the paper, so go do your thing. I gotta head back to my family's place anyway."

"Uncle Julian?" 

His brow twitched. The guy was ridiculously hot, but right now, he looked totally ticked off. 

Elara winced and corrected herself fast. "I mean... Julian?" 

Seriously, what was she supposed to call him? They were hitched, sure, but it was totally fake. "Babe" or "honey" made her stomach turn. And "Uncle Julian" was dead now. She only used that because of her ex, Ethan. It wasn't like they were actually related. She peeked at his face to see if he was gonna snap. Nope. He kept his mouth shut.

They reached his ride. "Need a lift?" he asked.

"Nah, I'm good. I'll just call an Uber," she said, waving a hand. "Seriously, don't sweat it."

He leaned against the door, looking like some high-fashion model. "You sure? I can tag along to your folks' place."

"No, really. I got this." 

He'd already done way too much by signing those papers. She wasn't about to push her luck. Honestly, pulling him out of danger back then wasn't some big hero move. She just reacted. She would've saved a stray dog the same way. But now? Cashing in that favor to force him into a marriage... Yeah, she felt like a total jerk.

***

Over at the Jewell mansion, Beatrix was pacing, face scrunched up. "Where the hell is she?"

"Mom, chill. She's probably just busy," Coraline said, all sweet and innocent. "I mean, yesterday's wedding was a total trainwreck. Elara is obsessed with Ethan. She had to be forced into this, right? No way she just fell out of love overnight." She watched her mom's face, then leaned in. "Look, you gotta stay cool and talk some sense into her. Julian Myers isn't some toy. What if she's actually trying to hook him for real now? You don't mess with a guy like that."

Coraline's eyes went dark. Julian was *her* prize. No way Elara was gonna just slide in and steal him. She'd spent years chasing that man. She even busted her ass at the family firm just to get on his radar. And what did she get? Zero. He never even looked at her. There was no freaking way he actually liked Elara.

Right then, the front door clicked. Elara walked in. 

Boom—every head snapped toward her. 

Walter slammed his phone shut. 

Beatrix glared, eyes burning. 

Victor Hayes stopped scrolling through his tablet and looked up. 

Leo Maxwell froze, his fingers stopping on his wooden beads. 

Even Cody Vance stopped taking selfies and dropped his phone. 

The three stepbrothers sat shoulder-to-shoulder on the sofa, staring her down like a jury ready to lock her up.

Coraline put on her fake-nice voice. "Elara! Where've you been? We've been waiting forever!"

Elara rolled her eyes. "Did I ask you to?"

"Hey, I didn't mean it like that..." Coraline whimpered, looking like she was gonna cry. "Mom's just stressed. She wants to talk. I'm sorry, okay?"

Classic. Same old crap. Coraline always flipped the script. Even when Elara did nothing wrong, Coraline's little puppy-dog act made Elara look like the bad guy. For years, Elara had begged them to believe her, trying to fight the lies. 

Screw that. Not today. 

If they wanted to treat her like a psycho, fine. She'd show them what a real psycho looked like.

###chapter 8
"Sorry for what, exactly? Spit it out. What're you actually apologizing for?" Elara let out a dry laugh. "Seriously, Coraline, why is 'sorry' your default? If you actually mean it, drop to your knees. Do it. Or is it just a cheap word to you? Like, if I slit your throat right now and said 'my bad,' would we be good?"

"Callie..." Coraline flinched, the color draining straight out of her face.

"Elara, what the hell is wrong with you? What did she ever do to deserve that?" Beatrix shoved herself between them, shielding Coraline. "How about you explain what went down at the wedding yesterday first?"

"What went down? You have eyes, don't you? I hitched myself to Julian. Got a problem with that?"

"Have you lost your damn mind?" Beatrix threw her hands up. "You think you can handle a guy like Julian? You're not even in his league. And what about Ethan? Weren't you, like, totally obsessed with him? Why do you screw up everything? You couldn't even keep your own fiancé."

The three brothers stood there like statues, giving Elara the side-eye. Walter finally broke the silence. "Elara, just tell us what happened yesterday. We have to clean up this mess, and we need the facts. Besides, we have to thank Mr. Myers properly."

"And Ethan? Did you piss him off again? You need to go crawl back and fix it. Otherwise, who the hell is ever going to marry you?"

Elara scanned Beatrix, then Walter, and back. Then, she just snorted. A real, loud laugh.

"Oh, so Ethan dumping me at the altar for his ex is *my* fault? And why am I too trash for Julian? Am I really that pathetic to you guys? What, do I need to beg on my knees for a husband? Is my life over just because Ethan bailed?"

Beatrix scowled, her patience wearing thin. "Elara, why do you have to be such a pain? You're always a disappointment!"

"Callie, come on, Mom and Dad are only trying to help!" Coraline whined.

"Save it." Elara's eyes went ice-cold. "If they actually cared, they'd hand over my inheritance." She thrust her open palm right in Coraline's face. "Where's my stuff? The earrings, the bracelet, the brooch Grandpa left me. You said you were just 'borrowing' them. Or was that a lie to keep them forever?"

She stepped in, her voice cutting like a blade. "You're adopted, Coraline. Know your place. My things aren't yours. My actual grandfather left them to *me*."

Coraline's face went white, then twisted in anger. "Fine! I'll go get your stupid jewelry!"

"Elara, you're not getting away that easily. Why are you treating your sister like garbage?" Out of nowhere, Beatrix threw a hard slap right at Elara's face.

But Elara was lightning. She snatched Beatrix's wrist mid-swing, locking it in a vice grip before it could connect.

"You always back the stray over your own flesh and blood. You're a joke." Elara shoved her hand away, sending Beatrix stumbling back onto the sofa.

"Elara! Are you trying to start a war in this house?" Beatrix screamed.

Elara rolled her eyes. "What, are you royalty now? Am I throwing a coup?" She glared at Coraline, pure disgust in her eyes. "Give me back my damn stuff."

Before Coraline could even open her mouth, Elara was already marching up the stairs. "Actually, forget it. I'll grab it myself. You'll probably 'lose' it on the way."

###chapter 9
"Elara, drop it! Seriously, what are you doing, looting your sister's closet? Look at this freaking disaster!"

Beatrix stood frozen at the door, hand slapped over her heart like she was dropping dead right there. The perfect, pink princess bedroom looked like a bomb had just gone off in it.

"Hey, Beatrix? Everything in this bag came straight from Grandpa to me," Elara snapped. "You guys stole my stuff and locked it up. That's looting. I'm just taking back my own damn property!"

She shoved another pile of clothes into her duffel, zipping it with a hard yank.

This whole room was packed with Elara's inheritance—sentimental pieces her grandfather left her before he died. But every single time Coraline whined about wanting something, Beatrix just snatched it and handed it over.

Hell, even this master bedroom used to belong to Elara.

She’d lived with the Jewells for a whole year before Coraline showed up. Back then, things were great. Beatrix and Walter actually acted like parents, and her three brothers treated her like their favorite person. She had the biggest room, the best clothes, the whole deal.

Then they adopted Coraline. Boom. Game over.

It started small. But slowly, Elara watched her family drift away, their entire lives suddenly spinning around Coraline. Pretty soon, they only threw birthday parties for Coraline. Everything Elara owned somehow ended up in Coraline's hands.

"Come on, you're the oldest, just let her have her way," they'd tell her.

"Stop being so immature. Grow up."

"Why can't you just listen for once?"

"Coraline is smarter than you, Elara. She's got actual talent."

They didn't know crap.

The joke was, Elara was way ahead of them in ways they couldn't even grasp. She’d practically carried them on her back, and they had no clue. But by the time she realized how bad things had gotten, the damage was done. Nobody believed a word she said anyway. It was always, "Oh, Coraline would never lie. Stop picking on her just because she actually behaves."

"Those were presents for Coraline!" Beatrix shrieked, her face turning red with rage. "How can you be so incredibly selfish and petty, Elara?"

"Oh, really? Did I sign a gift receipt?" Elara zipped her bag shut and looked up, flashing a cold smirk. "You gave my stuff away. Go buy her replacements. These belong to me, and you don't get to play charity with my things."

She grabbed the handle and hauled the heavy suitcase down the hall to her own room.

Her room was a joke compared to Coraline's massive, sun-drenched suite. It was a tiny closet of a space, barely fitting a twin bed and a cheap desk. Coraline got a huge walk-in closet; Elara got a creaky wardrobe that barely held three coats.

Looking around, the truth hit her hard. Almost everything she owned was just Coraline's old garbage—stuff her sister got bored of and tossed her way. They had never bought her a single thing she actually asked for.

Elara stared at the floor, her chest tightening. She’d spent years trying to make them love her, but they didn't give a damn. It still hurt. A heavy, dull ache settled deep in her chest.

How was it that she was their actual flesh and blood, yet Grandpa was the only one who ever gave a shit about her?

Whatever. Screw it. Some people just aren't meant to be loved by their families.

She threw her last few personal treasures into another bag. She didn't look back. She just grabbed her stuff and walked out.

"Hey, what's going on?" Walter called out from the bottom of the stairs, his forehead creasing as he stared up at her.

###chapter 10
"Get the hell out."

Elara scanned the room. Walter first. Then her three brothers. Finally, her eyes locked onto Beatrix and Coraline, who were hovering on the stairs.

She looked over at the massive family portrait on the wall. What a joke. Every single face was up there—except hers.

They shot that photo a year after Coraline moved in. Coraline had locked Elara in a room that morning, so the rest of them just went to the studio and posed without her.
